source_title: willemcvu/egmp-aa-ev-feat: Adding an energy model and live vehicle data to Android Auto, so Google Maps treats a Gen5W Hyundai/Kia like a native Google-built EV (charging stops, battery on arrival). - GitHub
source_excerpt:
Real EV routing in Google Maps on Android Auto for the Hyundai Ioniq 5's Gen5W head unit: battery % on arrival, charging stops, realistic charge times, and automatic battery preconditioning on the way to a fast charger. Built on NEMESIS and HMG Leafia Plus .
This modifies your infotainment system's files. The installer checks every file first and keeps a byte-for-byte backup, but you use it at your own risk. Not affiliated with Hyundai, Kia or Google.
Hyundai Ioniq 5 (US), Gen5W software NEEV.USA.0000.V015.012.260507
HMG Leafia Plus v1.0.5 installed first. This package builds on Leafia's modified Android Auto files; without exactly v1.0.5 the installer refuses and changes nothing.
EV routing: the head unit sends Maps a vehicle energy model with the battery's live energy, so Maps plans stops and shows arrival %.
Real capacity: usable capacity is learned from the BMS, not assumed from the new-car 77.4 kWh.
Cold weather: live outside temperature raises heating and rolling losses in the model.
Charge times: calibrated on real DC sessions and the car's own estimate, including the slow last 10–20 %.
Preconditioning: when the next stop is a charger over 50 kW within an hour, the car is asked to warm the battery. Turn it off with the car's own battery conditioning setting.
EV logs: driving and charging, whenever the head unit is on; copied to any USB drive with an egmp-aa-ev-logs folder; share them through an EV log issue .
Download the -usb.zip from Releases and copy its contents to an empty FAT32/exFAT drive.
Car on, plug the drive into a USB data port, tap Yes when NEMESIS asks. The head unit restarts when it's done.
It upgrades earlier versions in place. To uninstall: NEMESIS Manager (press NAV three times) → aa.ev.model → uninstall, then reboot; Leafia's files are restored exactly. Uninstall this before updating Leafia. More in the release's README.txt .
The release contains no Hyundai or Google files, only small binary deltas that lpatch applies to your unit's own files.
The head unit records a small log whenever the car is on, driving or charging: battery energy and power, speed, temperatures, climate, charging and Maps' route plan. No location, no full VIN, no times of day. It keeps up to 100 MB, oldest first out.
Make a folder named egmp-aa-ev-logs at the top level of any FAT32/exFAT USB drive.
With the car on, plug the drive into the USB data port. Within about 20 seconds a pop-up says how many logs were copied ("… Safe to remove").
Open an EV log issue and drag the egmp-*.csv files from that folder into it. Issues are public.
Logs from different cars, climates and battery ages are what improve the energy model most. Format details: LOGGING .
The build patches files from your own head unit (not in this repo); see HANDOFF for what goes in private/ and the toolchain.
NEMESIS (xwtk), HMG Leafia Plus (including lpatch , GPL-3.0), aa-proxy-rs , open-android-auto , gen5w-preconditioning .
Adding an energy model and live vehicle data to Android Auto, so Google Maps treats a Gen5W Hyundai/Kia like a native Google-built EV (charging stops, battery on arrival).
